continuity_scope: A character-layer pass limited to Robin Hobb's Assassin's Apprentice, the first Farseer Trilogy novel, using the Del Rey paperback published 29 August 2023, ISBN 9780593722824, 464 pages. It is neither a record of the full Farseer trilogy nor of the several distinct Realm of the Elderlings subseries and time layers. Narrative claims use chapter number/title locators rather than pagination transferred from other editions.

work_or_witnesses.edition: Del Rey paperback, 29 August 2023, ISBN 9780593722824, 464 pages
Author's official Realm of the Elderlings reading-order page; Farseer publication context

coverage_rule: Include Fitz; his named individual guardians, teachers, royal patrons and rivals; named individual friends/love interest; the named individual Mountain Kingdom counterpart needed for its distinct political-cultural term; and Nosy because the individually named dog is a dramatic agent in the novel's initial Wit event. The 11-individual cohort is bounded to central Book One action, not every named person or animal.
omissions: Royal Assassin, Assassin's Quest, the Liveship Traders, Tawny Man, Rain Wild, Fitz and the Fool, all other Realm of the Elderlings works, and adaptations/illustrated editions as separate witnesses.
The Six Duchies, Buckkeep, the Farseer dynasty, the Skill, Wit, Forging, coteries, royal offices, peoples, raiders, artifacts, and narratorial functions as nodes; they remain terms or dimensions.

Named but non-cohort individuals including Chivalry, Patience, Rurisk, August, Serene, and minor court, town, voyage, or raid figures; named animals other than Nosy are excluded from this specific cohort.
Later-series identities, outcomes, family relations, political changes, and retrospective explanations not established by this one novel.
uncertainties: Fitz narrates retrospectively in first person. His account offers close access to his perceptions and memories but is not omniscient evidence for other characters' intentions, interiority, or unobserved events.
The selected print edition differs from older US and ebook pagination. Chapter titles/numbers are used as stable locators; page-specific verification must use the ISBN 9780593722824 printing.
Skill, Wit, Forging, Farseer naming, and Mountain Kingdom terms are source-specific and not direct equivalents of generic psychic powers, animal classes, corruption mechanics, or real-world cultures.
The novel includes coercion, abuse, violence, and sexual violence; records use concise, non-graphic paraphrase and mark major spoilers.
evidence_basis: Primary claims are tied to the declared printed novel by exact chapter title/number. Penguin Random House supplies edition metadata and an official synopsis; Robin Hobb's official works page establishes the Farseer trilogy's distinct place within the larger, multi-series Realm of the Elderlings. No fan wiki, Wikipedia, or plot-summary source is used as canonical evidence.
